name: Data Analyzer: Too many wrong API keys in a row are locked out with HTTP 429
objective: Proves a caller cannot keep guessing keys: after the allowed number of failures, further wrong keys are refused with HTTP 429 (too many requests) instead of 403.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send 8 analysis requests in a row, each with a different wrong API key.
steps.data: 8 requests with keys wrong-0 to wrong-7 and a tiny made-up CSV
steps.expected: The first 5 answers are HTTP 403 (forbidden); the last 3 are HTTP 429.

name: Data Analyzer: The lockout response tells the caller how long to wait (60 seconds)
objective: Proves the lockout answer carries a Retry-After header so a well-behaved client knows when to try again.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Make 5 wrong-key requests, then a 6th wrong-key request.
steps.data: Wrong keys wrong-0 to wrong-4, then wrong-again
steps.expected: The 6th answer is HTTP 429 and its Retry-After header is exactly 60 (seconds).

name: Data Analyzer: On a shared address, the correct key still works after a lockout; wrong keys stay blocked
objective: Proves that when many users may share one network address (caller's own address unknown), a legitimate user with the right key is never locked out by someone else's guessing.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Make 5 wrong-key requests to reach the limit.
steps.expected: Each is refused (counted as a failure).

steps.action: Send one request with the correct key, then one with a wrong key.
steps.expected: The correct key gets HTTP 200 (served). The wrong key gets HTTP 429 with Retry-After 60.

name: Data Analyzer: Correct API keys are never counted as failed attempts
objective: Proves normal use with the right key, however often, never triggers a lockout.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send 12 requests with the correct key.

name: Data Analyzer: Requests with no API key get 401 and do not cause a lockout
objective: Proves that leaving out the key is reported as 'not authorised' and is not counted as a wrong guess.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send 8 requests with no API key header.
Then send one request with the correct key.

name: Data Analyzer: Failed attempts are counted separately for each caller address
objective: Proves one address being locked out does not lock out a different address.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Make 5 wrong-key requests from the test client's own address.
steps.expected: Failures are recorded against that address.

steps.action: Call the lockout check directly for a different, made-up address (203.0.113.9) and for the offending address.
steps.data: Two stand-in requests that differ only by address
steps.expected: The different address passes the check without any error; the offending address is refused with HTTP 429.

name: Data Analyzer: The allowed number of wrong attempts can be changed by a setting
objective: Proves the limit is read from the environment setting rather than fixed in the code.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Change the limit setting to 2, reset counters, and send 4 wrong-key requests.
steps.data: Setting DATA_ANALYZER_AUTH_FAIL_LIMIT=2; keys w0 to w3
steps.expected: The answers are 403, 403, 429, 429 in that order. (The test only changes the limit; it does not check the window length.)

name: Data Analyzer: The health check keeps working while a caller is locked out
objective: Proves monitoring of the service is not blocked by a key-guessing lockout.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Make 6 wrong-key requests, then ask the health endpoint for its status.
steps.data: 6 wrong keys; GET of the health address with no key

name: Data Analyzer: A key containing non-English characters gets a clean 403, not a crash
objective: Proves an oddly encoded key is rejected politely instead of causing a server error.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send a request whose API key header is the accented word 'cafe' with an accent.
steps.data: Key 'café' sent as raw Latin-1 bytes
steps.expected: HTTP 403, and the error message is exactly 'Invalid credentials provided.'

name: Data Analyzer: The log records a failed login but never writes the wrong key itself
objective: Proves the guessed key does not leak into the service log.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key. The allowed number of wrong-key attempts is set to 5 within a 60-second window and the counters are reset first. No trusted-proxy setting is configured, so the caller's address is the one the test client connects from. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send one request with the wrong key 'very-secret-wrong-guess' while capturing warning-level log lines.
steps.expected: A log line containing 'auth_failure' exists; no log line contains the guessed key text. (The test checks the key is absent, not that the client address is present.)
